content:
# Da Nang to Nha Trang Coastal EV Road Trip: Quy Nhon, Beaches & Charging Guide 2026

**Last updated: June 7, 2026**

The 530 km coastal corridor from Da Nang to Nha Trang is arguably Vietnam's most beautiful EV road trip. While the Hanoi–HCMC north–south route gets all the attention, this central coast stretch packs the highest density of pristine beaches, mountain-meets-sea driving, and emerging EV infrastructure anywhere in Southeast Asia.

And in 2026, it's electrifyingly ready. V-Green has rolled out 99 new fast-charging stations across Vietnam this year, including critical new installments at Quy Nhon, Tuy Hoa, and Sa Huynh — filling the last remaining gaps on this coastal route. What was a range-anxiety stretch in 2024 is now a relaxed, beach-hopping EV paradise.

This guide covers the complete 4-day itinerary, every charging stop, the best beaches you'd miss without knowing about them, and why Quy Nhon (not Da Nang, not Nha Trang) might be the highlight of your trip.

---

## Route Overview

| Detail | Info |
|--------|------|
| **Total distance** | ~530 km (Da Nang → Nha Trang via QL1 + DT639 coastal road) |
| **Recommended duration** | 4 days (3 nights) |
| **Driving days** | 3 driving days (2–3.5 hours per day, plus stops) |
| **Charging stops** | 3–4 (Quy Nhon, Tuy Hoa, possibly Sa Huynh) |
| **Total charging cost** | VND 400,000–650,000 (USD $16–27) |
| **Toll road cost** | VND 250,000 (USD $10) — Hai Van Tunnel if coming from Da Nang |
| **Best season** | February–August (dry season on central coast) |
| **Avoid** | October–December (typhoon season — landslides possible on coastal roads) |

### Route at a Glance

**Day 1:** Da Nang → Hoi An → Tam Ky → Sa Huynh → Quy Nhon (250 km)
**Day 2:** Quy Nhon day — beaches, Eo Gio, and Hon Kho Island
**Day 3:** Quy Nhon → Tuy Hoa → Nha Trang (230 km)
**Day 4:** Nha Trang day — islands, VinWonders, or beach time

### Why Drive This Route in an EV?

1. **Short hops, minimal range anxiety** — No segment exceeds 200 km without a charging option
2. **V-Green's 2026 expansion fills all gaps** — Quy Nhon (new 180 kW ultra-fast), Tuy Hoa, and Sa Huynh now have reliable DC fast charging
3. **Free charging for VinFast owners** — VinFast's free charging program in Vietnam runs through December 2027 — every kWh at V-Green stations is free for VinFast EVs
4. **Lower operating cost than petrol** — Even on paid public charging, expect VND 500,000 total for the route vs. VND 1,500,000+ for a petrol car

---

## Charging Infrastructure Along the Route

### V-Green (VinFast) — The Backbone

V-Green now operates over 4,000 charging ports across Vietnam. On the Da Nang–Nha Trang corridor, key stations:

| Location | Type | Power | Connectors | Status |
|----------|------|-------|------------|--------|
| **Da Nang** (Son Tra) | DC Fast | 60 kW | CCS2, VinFast prop | Operational ✅ |
| **Hoi An** (An Bang) | DC Fast | 60 kW | CCS2 | Operational ✅ |
| **Tam Ky** | DC Fast | 60 kW | CCS2 | Operational ✅ |
| **Sa Huynh** | DC Fast | 60 kW | CCS2 | NEW 2026 ✅ |
| **Quy Nhon** (City Center) | DC Ultra-Fast | **180 kW** | CCS2 | NEW 2026 ✅ |
| **Tuy Hoa** | DC Fast | 60 kW | CCS2 | NEW 2026 ✅ |
| **Nha Trang** (multiple) | DC Fast + Ultra-Fast | 60–180 kW | CCS2 | Operational ✅ |

**Note for non-VinFast EVs:** All V-Green stations now support CCS2. The VinFast proprietary plug was phased out at new installations in late 2025. Older stations may still require an adapter — carry a CCS2 adapter to be safe.

### EVOne — Premium Backup

EVOne operates 120 kW rapid chargers at:
- **Da Nang** — Vincom Center
- **Quy Nhon** — Muong Thanh Hotel
- **Nha Trang** — several locations near the beachfront

EVOne charges a premium (VND 4,500–5,500/kWh) but is a reliable backup if V-Green stations are occupied.

### Destination Charging at Hotels

This is where the central coast truly shines. Many mid-range and luxury hotels in Quy Nhon and Nha Trang now offer free Level 2 destination charging for guests. We've listed the best EV-friendly hotels in each section below.

---

## Day 1: Da Nang → Hoi An → Quy Nhon — The Long Drive (250 km)

**Drive time:** 4.5–5 hours (with Hoi An stop)  
**Charging needed:** 1 stop minimum (Hoi An or Tam Ky)  
**Best EV range for this day:** 350+ km WLTP

### Start: Da Nang

Pick up your EV in Da Nang — either from VinFast Rental (official, booking 2–3 days ahead) or a local agency. Your VF8 or VF9 should start the day at 90–100% charge. No need to top up in Da Nang — you have plenty of range for the day's driving.

**Quick Da Nang tip:** If you haven't explored Da Nang, spend the morning at **My Khe Beach** or the **Son Tra Peninsula** (Monkey Mountain). The drive up Son Tra in an EV is a perfect warm-up — quiet electric motor, winding coastal road, and spectacular views over the city.

### Stop 1: Hoi An (30 km, 45 min)

Hoi An is a 30-minute drive south of Da Nang via the coastal road. The ancient town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of Vietnam's most photogenic destinations.

**Charging:** V-Green at An Bang Beach (60 kW DC). Park your car, walk 5 minutes into the Old Town for lunch at **Morning Glory** (try the cao lầu and white rose dumplings), and your EV will be ready by the time you finish.

**What to do (2–3 hours):**
- Walk the Old Town's lantern-lit streets
- Visit the Japanese Covered Bridge (18th century)
- Thu Bon River boat ride (VND 100,000 per person)
- Tailor-made clothing — Hoi An is famous for 24-hour custom tailoring

**EV tip:** An Bang Beach also has Level 2 destination chargers at several resorts if you want to stay overnight. Consider staying here if 250 km in one day feels like too much.

### Stop 2: Tam Ky (75 km from Hoi An, 1.5 hours)

Tam Ky is a quiet provincial capital, not a tourist town. But it has a V-Green station that's perfect for a mid-route top-up if needed. The station is at the PetroVietnam petrol station just off QL1.

**Charging:** V-Green 60 kW DC. 15–20 minutes for a meaningful top-up.

**Alternative:** Skip Tam Ky if your EV has 350+ km range. The next guaranteed charging is at Sa Huynh, 120 km south.

### Stop 3: Sa Huynh (60 km from Tam Ky, 1 hour)

Sa Huynh is one of the 2026 V-Green expansion stations — a critical new addition that closes the former 180 km gap between Tam Ky and Quy Nhon. This is a small coastal town known for its salt fields, not tourism. But the charging station is clean, modern, and reliable.

**Charging:** V-Green 60 kW DC (NEW 2026). Take 20 min, grab a coffee at the adjacent rest stop.

**Photo opportunity:** The salt fields at sunset are otherworldly — flat white planes reflecting the sky like a Vietnamese Salar de Uyuni.

### Arrive: Quy Nhon (90 km from Sa Huynh, 1.5 hours)

Welcome to the most underrated beach city in Vietnam. Quy Nhon has been called "the new Da Nang" by travel writers, but that undersells it. Think: Da Nang's charm from 10 years ago, before the high-rises and crowds.

**Charging at arrival:** V-Green's new 180 kW ultra-fast station in the city center (Tran Hung Dao Street). Charge from 20% to 80% in under 15 minutes — barely enough time to check your messages.

**EV-friendly hotels in Quy Nhon:**
| Hotel | Charging | Price/night | Notes |
|-------|----------|------------|-------|
| Avani Quy Nhon Resort | Level 2 (free) | VND 2,500,000+ | Beachfront, 5-star, 2 EV chargers |
| Muong Thanh Quy Nhon | EVOne 120 kW (guest rate) | VND 1,000,000+ | City center, reliable charging |
| FLC Quy Nhon Beach Resort | Level 2 (free) | VND 1,800,000+ | Huge resort, 4 chargers |
| Life Resort Quy Nhon | Level 2 (free) | VND 3,000,000+ | Boutique luxury, 1 charger |

---

## Day 2: Explore Quy Nhon — Beaches, The Eo Gio, and Hon Kho Island

**No driving day.** Charge overnight at your hotel or visit the V-Green ultra-fast station in the morning.

Quy Nhon is the highlight many travelers miss. The city faces east onto the South China Sea, with a 40 km coastline of pristine beaches, granite headlands, and calm bays.

### Must-Visit Spots in Quy Nhon

**1. Eo Gio (The Wind's Pass)** — 20 km north of the city. A dramatic granite headland with a coastal walking trail, sea arch, and turquoise waters. Entry is VND 30,000. Go early (7 AM) to beat the heat and the tour buses. The walk takes 45 minutes to an hour.

**2. Hon Kho Island** — A 15-minute boat ride from Quy Nhon's port. White sand beach, calm swimming, and excellent fresh seafood (the grilled squid is legendary). Boat rental: VND 300,000 for a small group.

**3. Ky Co Beach** — The most photographed beach in the area. White sand, jade water, and dramatic mountain backdrop. Best accessed by a 10-minute boat ride. Entry: VND 50,000. Weekends get busy — visit on a weekday if possible.

**4. Quy Nhon City Center** — The evening promenade along Xuan Dieu Street comes alive at sunset. Street food stalls sell bánh xèo (crispy pancakes), fresh spring rolls, and seafood. Try **Bánh Hỏi Lòng Heo** (grilled pork with fine rice noodles) at the night market.

**5. Thap Doi (Twin Towers)** — Ruins of the Cham civilization, right in the city center. Not as impressive as My Son, but free and a 15-minute walk from the beachfront.

### Where to Eat in Quy Nhon

- **Quán Ốc Phố Biển** — The best seafood in town. Grilled scallops with spring onion oil, squid satay, and crab hotpot. VND 200,000–400,000 per person.
- **Bánh Xèo Bà Năm** — Legendary crispy pancakes. VND 25,000 each. Go hungry.
- **Nhà Hàng Hoa Sứ** — Upscale Vietnamese in a colonial-style villa. VND 500,000 per person for a feast.

### Charging for Tomorrow

Plug in at the V-Green 180 kW station before dinner. Alternatively, your hotel may offer free overnight Level 2 charging. The next day is 230 km of driving — you want 90%+ to start.

---

## Day 3: Quy Nhon → Tuy Hoa → Nha Trang (230 km)

**Drive time:** 4 hours total  
**Charging needed:** 1 stop (Tuy Hoa)

### Morning: Quy Nhon to Tuy Hoa (110 km, 2 hours)

The coastal road from Quy Nhon to Tuy Hoa is the most scenic stretch of the entire trip. The QL1 hugs the coastline, with continuous ocean views, fishing villages, and coconut-fringed beaches.

**Don't miss:** Đầm Ô Loan (Ô Loan Lagoon) — about 30 km south of Quy Nhon. A vast, mirror-like lagoon surrounded by low mountains. It's a classic Vietnamese landscape painting brought to life. Pull over at the viewpoint on the bridge.

### Stop: Tuy Hoa (110 km from Quy Nhon)

Tuy Hoa is a rising star on Vietnam's tourist map — largely because of its spectacular **Vung Ro Bay** and **Mui Dien Lighthouse** (the easternmost point of mainland Vietnam, where the sunrise hits first).

**Charging:** V-Green 60 kW DC (NEW 2026). Located at the petrol station on Highway 1 just before the city center. 20 minutes for 10%–60% on a VF8.

**What to do while charging (1–2 hours):**
- **Vung Ro Bay** — 15 km south. A stunning, sheltered bay with emerald water and jungle-clad mountains. Boat tours available for VND 250,000.
- **Mui Dien Lighthouse** (Dai Lanh) — 40-minute drive east. The first sunrise in Vietnam. If you're an early riser, arrive before 5 AM. The lighthouse was built by the French in 1890.
- **Nhan Tower** — A Cham tower right in the middle of Tuy Hoa city. Good for a quick photo stop.

### Afternoon: Tuy Hoa to Nha Trang (120 km, 2 hours)

The final stretch is a straight shot down QL1 — flatter terrain, less dramatic coastal scenery, but dotted with fishing villages and salt fields. The road is good quality, well-lit, and has frequent rest stops.

**Charging caution:** There is no charging station between Tuy Hoa and Nha Trang (the next V-Green is in Nha Trang itself). Ensure your EV has at least 30% range before leaving Tuy Hoa. Most EVs with 350+ km WLTP can do this segment without issue.

### Arrive: Nha Trang

Nha Trang is Vietnam's most famous beach city — and yes, it's touristy. But for good reason: 6 km of golden beach, clear water, a backdrop of rugged mountains, and some of the best island hopping in Southeast Asia.

**Charging on arrival:** Multiple V-Green stations in Nha Trang:
- **V-Green Nha Trang 1** — Tran Phu Street (180 kW ultra-fast ✅)
- **V-Green Nha Trang 2** — near VinWonders entrance (60 kW DC)
- **EVOne** — multiple locations (120 kW, premium pricing)

**EV-friendly hotels in Nha Trang:**
| Hotel | Charging | Price/night | Notes |
|-------|----------|------------|-------|
| Sheraton Nha Trang | Level 2 (free) | VND 2,200,000+ | City center, 2 chargers |
| Mia Resort Nha Trang | Level 2 (free) | VND 3,000,000+ | North beach, quiet |
| Vinpearl Nha Trang | Level 2 (free) | VND 2,800,000+ | Resort island, ferry access |
| Muong Thanh Nha Trang | EVOne 120 kW | VND 900,000+ | Budget-friendly |

---

## Day 4: Nha Trang — Islands, VinWonders, or Pure Relaxation

**Optional driving:** 0 km. Leave your EV plugged in and enjoy Nha Trang on foot or by boat.

### Top Things to Do in Nha Trang

**1. Island Hopping Tour (full day)** — The classic Nha Trang experience. Visit Hon Mun (coral reef snorkeling), Hon Tam (beach resort), and Hon Mieu (aquarium). Tours cost VND 300,000–500,000 including lunch. Book through your hotel or a reputable operator.

**2. VinWonders Nha Trang** — A massive amusement park on Hon Tre Island, accessible by the world's longest cable car over the sea (3.3 km). Entry: VND 880,000 adults, VND 660,000 children. Includes water park, aquarium, roller coaster, and cultural shows.

**3. Po Nagar Cham Towers** — A 7th–12th century Cham temple complex on a hill north of the city. Beautiful at sunset. Entry: VND 30,000.

**4. Mud Baths** — Nha Trang is famous for its mineral mud baths. Try **Thap Ba Hot Springs** or **100 Egg Mud Bath** — both family-friendly and affordable (VND 150,000–300,000).

**5. Nha Trang Night Market** — Every evening from 6 PM on Tran Phu Street. Great for souvenir shopping, street food, and people-watching.

### Where to Eat in Nha Trang

- **Lac Canh Restaurant** — Nha Trang institution since 1970. BBQ beef and squid grilled at your table. VND 150,000–300,000 per person.
- **Nha Trang Seafood** — Truong Son Street seafood street. Pick your live seafood from tanks, they grill it for you. The garlic butter scallops are essential.
- **Xôi Cô Ba** — Sticky rice with pork floss and pâté. The perfect VND 20,000 breakfast.

---

## Extended Options

### Add Day 5: Nha Trang → Da Lat (3.5 days)

If you have extra time, Vietnam's cool mountain retreat is just 135 km west of Nha Trang. The drive climbs from sea level to 1,500 m through pine forests and coffee plantations — stunning, and an excellent EV range test. See our [separate guide](/blog/vietnam-ev-road-trip-ho-chi-minh-city-to-da-lat-complete-guide) for the full Da Lat itinerary.

### Add Day 5–6: Nha Trang → Phan Thiet (Mui Ne) → Ho Chi Minh City (2 more days)

Continue south for 260 km to Phan Thiet (Mui Ne's sand dunes and beach resorts), then 200 km on to HCMC. This is covered in the [north–south Vietnam guide](/blog/vietnam-ev-charging-guide-2026).

---

## Essential Planning Tips

### Renting an EV in Vietnam

- **VinFast Rental** — Official VinFast rental through their dealer network. Available in Da Nang, Nha Trang, HCMC, and Hanoi. Requires booking 2–3 days ahead.
- **Mioto** — Vietnam's Turo equivalent. Peer-to-peer VinFast rentals starting from VND 1,200,000/day.
- **Local agencies** — Most car rental agencies now carry VinFast vehicles. Expect VND 1,500,000–2,500,000/day for a VF8.

**Required documents:** International Driving Permit (IDP) recognized under Vietnam's 2025 updated traffic laws, OR a Vietnamese driving license. Rental companies typically require a deposit (VND 20–50 million, refundable).

### Charging App Essentials

Download these before you go:
- **V-Green App** — Find all V-Green stations, check real-time availability, start charging (iOS/Android)
- **EVOne App** — Premium charging network, useful backup
- **PlugShare** — Community-verified charging locations, including hotel destination chargers

### Money Tips

- **Total trip cost (charging):** VND 400,000–650,000 ($16–27 USD) — free if you're in a VinFast
- **Total trip cost (tolls):** ~VND 250,000 ($10 USD)
- **Daily budget (food + activities):** VND 500,000–1,500,000 ($20–60 USD) per person
- **Cash is still king** for street food, markets, and smaller charging stations. ATMs are common in all cities.

### When to Go

| Season | Months | Verdict |
|--------|--------|--------|
| 🌤 Dry | Feb–Aug | Perfect. Clear skies, calm seas, 28–35°C |
| 🌧 Rainy | Sep–Jan | Risk. October–December is typhoon season on central coast. Possible landslides on DT639. |

### What to Pack

- CCS2 charging adapter (for older V-Green stations)
- Vietnamese SIM card with data (for charging app navigation)
- A long-sleeve layer — air conditioning in Vietnamese malls is aggressive
- Sunscreen and a hat — the coastal sun is intense
- A reusable water bottle — many charging stations have filtered water

---

## FAQ

### Can I drive this route in a non-VinFast EV?

Yes. All new V-Green stations use CCS2 connectors, and the EVOne network is exclusively CCS2. EU and Chinese EVs (MG, BYD, Ora) are well-supported. Tesla owners will need a CCS2 adapter (available at V-Green stations).

### Is the Hai Van Pass EV-friendly?

Yes — and it's spectacular in an EV. The regenerative braking on the descent saves significant battery. The pass adds 30 minutes compared to the tunnel but offers views you won't forget. The road is well-paved in 2026. Just watch for trucks on blind corners.

### Are there charging stations at every stop?

2026 update: Yes, all major stops now have charging. New stations at Sa Huynh, Quy Nhon (180 kW), and Tuy Hoa have closed the gaps. The longest stretch without charging is Tuy Hoa → Nha Trang (120 km) — easily within range of any EV.

### Where do I charge in Quy Nhon?

The new V-Green 180 kW ultra-fast station on Tran Hung Dao Street is the best option. Hotel destination charging is available at Avani Quy Nhon, FLC Quy Nhon, and Life Resort.

### Can I charge at my hotel in Nha Trang?

Most 4–5 star hotels in Nha Trang now offer free Level 2 charging. Sheraton, Mia Resort, and Vinpearl all have dedicated EV chargers. Confirm when booking.

### What if all charging stations are occupied?

Vietnam's EV adoption is still early (EVs are ~5% of new car sales in 2026), so station congestion is rare outside of Tet (Lunar New Year). Weekday charging is typically quiet. Plan around Tet (January–February) for the busiest charging conditions.

---

## The Bottom Line

Da Nang to Nha Trang is the perfect weekend-to-midweek EV road trip in Vietnam. At 530 km across 4 days, it's manageable, relaxed, and packed with variety — from Hai Van Pass mountain views to Quy Nhon's undiscovered beaches to Nha Trang's world-class island hopping.

The 2026 V-Green expansion has transformed this route from a bold adventure into a comfortable, family-friendly road trip. Quy Nhon alone is worth the drive — it's the kind of place you visit for a day and stay for three.
